question: What is the structure of the feed-forward block inside a transformer layer?
options: Two linear projections with a non-linearity (e.g., GELU or SwiGLU) between them
A single linear projection with no activation
Just attention applied a second time

question: Why is the FFN typically widened (e.g., 4x d_model) in the middle?
options: To give the layer more capacity to compute non-linear combinations of features before projecting back
GPUs run faster on wider tensors regardless of computation
It's needed for backpropagation to work

question: Is the FFN applied per-token or across the sequence?
options: Per-token — the same FFN runs independently on each position
It mixes information across all positions
It only runs on the first token
It's applied between layers, not within them
